title: Signadot Is Now Available on AWS Marketplace
summary: Buy Signadot through AWS Marketplace: self-serve the Business tier or take an Enterprise private offer, billed on your AWS invoice.
body_markdown:
Signadot is now listed on[AWS Marketplace](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-d4g65y3cpqvvw) . You can subscribe to the Business tier from your AWS account, or take an Enterprise plan as a private offer with terms we agree on together. Either way, Signadot is billed on your AWS invoice.


The product is the same one you would buy from us directly. What changes is how you pay for it: through an AWS account your company has already approved, and against AWS spend you may have already committed.


## How to procure Signadot on AWS Marketplace


The listing offers two ways to buy. Teams that want to start now can subscribe to the Business tier on their own. Teams that need more capacity or custom terms get an Enterprise private offer.


### Business Tier (self-serve)


Subscribe from the[AWS Marketplace listing](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-d4g65y3cpqvvw) , choose a 1-month or 12-month contract, and set up your Signadot organization. The 12-month contract saves 10%. There is no sales call and no order form.


It is the same Business plan as on our[pricing page](https://www.signadot.com/pricing/) . The base plan costs $250 a month and includes:


- 100 Sandboxes created per month
- 200 test invocations per month
- 15 concurrent devboxes
- 3 Kubernetes clusters
- 5 resource plugins
- Support through the Signadot Community Slack and email


As usage grows, you add capacity in blocks. Each add-on is priced on its own, so you pay only for the capacity you need.


Add-on What it adds Price per month


Environments 50 more Sandbox creations a month, up to 400 in all $300


Test invocations 100 more test invocations a month $50


Devboxes 5 more concurrent devboxes $200


SSO Single sign-on with your identity provider $250


What they are:


- **Sandbox.** A lightweight ephemeral environment that runs in your cluster and only deploys the services under test. It is counted once, when it is created. Updates do not count against your quota.
- **Test invocation.** One Job or SmartTest run against a Sandbox, however many tests run inside it.
- **Devbox.** A developer or agent’s workstation or cloud development environment (CDE) connected to the cluster, so they can run a service locally against real dependencies. The limit is how many are connected at the same time.


### Enterprise Tier (private offer)


Enterprise plans are sold as AWS Marketplace[private offers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/buyerguide/buyer-private-offers.html) . We agree on pricing and terms with you, then send the offer straight to your AWS account. Your team reviews and accepts it in the AWS console, and Signadot is billed on the same invoice as the rest of your AWS infrastructure.


An Enterprise plan adds unlimited clusters and resource plugins, SSO, multi-year contracts, a dedicated Slack channel with premium support, and a guided pilot. If you are already an Enterprise customer, your account team can move your current contract to a private offer.


## Why buy through AWS?


For many engineering orgs, the slowest part of adopting a new tool is not the technical evaluation. It is procurement: onboarding a new vendor, setting up a payment method, and routing another invoice for approval. Buying through AWS Marketplace removes most of those steps.


- **Your AWS commitment goes further.** Signadot carries the Deployed on AWS designation, so Marketplace spend can count toward an existing AWS commitment, such as an Enterprise Discount Program agreement. Budget you have already committed to AWS can pay for Signadot.
- **No new vendor to onboard.** AWS is already an approved vendor at your company. There is no new supplier record, no new payment method, and no separate invoice to approve.
- **One bill.** Signadot shows up in AWS Billing and Cost Management next to your[Amazon EKS](https://aws.amazon.com/eks/) clusters and everything else you run on AWS.


## How it works


The Signadot operator installs in your Kubernetes cluster, on Amazon EKS or any conformant Kubernetes distribution, and connects to the Signadot control plane. Your workloads stay in your own AWS account.


Each Sandbox deploys only the services a change touches and shares everything else with the stable versions already running in the cluster. Sandboxes are ready in seconds and isolated from each other, so hundreds of changes can be tested in parallel without copying your stack.


Developers, CI pipelines, and coding agents create Sandboxes on demand. Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex connect through the[Signadot MCP server](https://www.signadot.com/docs/integrations/mcp) , and any agent that can run shell commands can use the CLI. Jobs run your Playwright, Cypress, and end-to-end suites inside each Sandbox, and Plans give agents and CI the same reusable checks. The[Signadot platform overview](https://www.signadot.com/product/platform/) covers the rest.


## Get started


- Subscribe to the Business tier from the[AWS Marketplace listing](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-d4g65y3cpqvvw) .
- For Enterprise pricing, custom terms, or to move an existing contract to AWS billing, emailsales@signadot.com and we will send a private offer to your AWS account.
- To try Signadot first,[sign up for the free tier](https://www.signadot.com/signup/) , which includes one Kubernetes cluster and one resource plugin.
